properties.figure: Figure 1 (left panel, geographic map with Shear/Extensional/Compressional Zone outlines)
properties.provenance: This polygon is a RECONSTRUCTION of the zone outline visible in the published Figure 1 raster, not the authors' original GIS/digitizing data (which is not publicly available). It was produced by calibrating a high-resolution PDF-page render against the figure's own axis tick marks (23-31E / 33-43N), then tracing the red-dotted 'Shear Zone' line color (RGB ~175,34,32) via a mix of automated connected-component pixel analysis and manual verification against zoomed crops. Some vertices (see vertex_notes) are medium-confidence visual reconstructions, not exact original coordinates.
properties.geometry_method: calibrated pixel tracing (PyMuPDF page render at 8x scale, axis calibrated from tick-mark pixel positions; red-dotted line color-thresholded, connected-component isolated, corner positions refined by row-by-row pixel sampling for the Zone 6/7 shared-boundary section)
properties.confidence: mixed -- see vertex_notes for per-vertex confidence (high/medium-high/medium)
properties.known_limitation: Vertex 8 (NE corner of Zone 1, ~30.2E/41.0N) sits in a zone of coastline/frame-edge ambiguity and was deliberately NOT chased to sub-pixel precision; treat as approximate. Coastal-tracing vertices (2-6, 15-16) are smoothed from a chain of pixel fragments along the coastline, not exact coastline-following coordinates.
properties.verified_against: Zones 1,2,3,4,7,8,9 confirmed enclosed by this polygon; Zones 5,6 (Extensional) confirmed excluded, in a rendered overlay check against the source figure (2026-09-10)

properties.source_full: Oncel, A.O. and Wilson, T. (2004), Correlation of seismotectonic variables and GPS strain measurements in western Turkey, J. Geophys. Res., 109, B11306, doi:10.1029/2004JB003101
properties.figure: Figure 1 (left panel, geographic map with Shear/Extensional/Compressional Zone outlines)
properties.provenance: This geometry is a RECONSTRUCTION of the orange-dashed 'Extensional Zone' outline visible in the published Figure 1 raster, not the authors' original GIS/digitizing data. Produced from the SAME calibrated, north-up render used for the Shear Zone (calibration: x0=62.5px/lon0=23.0E/sx=207.2px per degree, y0=62.5px/lat0=43.0N/sy=199.8px per degree), by color-isolating the orange line (RGB target 199,129,35, tolerance 35), row/column band-scanning to locate corner pixels, and cross-checking every candidate corner against zoomed crops of the source image before accepting it. No smoothing, interpolation, or geometric regularization was applied -- vertices follow the actually-detected line pixels, including its real, non-rectilinear character. Where this polygon shares a boundary with the already-approved Shear Zone (the Zone 6/7 edge), the exact Shear Zone vertex coordinates were reused verbatim rather than re-measured, to guarantee a zero-gap shared edge.
properties.geometry_method: calibrated pixel tracing (same 2004_geo_panel_rot.png render and calibration as Shear Zone); orange line color-thresholded and isolated from an OR-combined multi-row/column band scan (dash-gap tolerant); corner longitudes/latitudes read directly from band-scan cluster centroids; ambiguous junctions (Zone 18 east closure) additionally checked against 2x-upscaled visual crops before being accepted
properties.topology_note: The source figure draws the Extensional Zone as TWO separate, non-overlapping pieces that only touch, not one single simple ring. This is represented as a MultiPolygon: Part A = zones 6,5,11,10,15,17,16,12,13 (the main NE block, sharing its NW top edge with Shear Zone's zone-7 boundary); Part B = zones 18,19 (a thin wedge/strip south of Part A, touching Part A at two shared vertices (26.47,36.96) and (27.70,36.96) but not merged into a single ring, because the drawn dashed line genuinely does not close as one simple polygon at those points).
properties.confidence: mixed -- see vertex_notes for per-vertex/per-part confidence (high/medium-high/medium)
properties.known_limitation: Part B vertex index 4 (~27.80E/36.70N, the SE closing corner of the Zone 18/19 wedge, where the orange Extensional line transitions to the white Compressional line) could NOT be pinned down to better than roughly +/-0.1-0.2 degrees: the upper (lat~37.00) and lower (lat~36.66) branches of the dashed line converge in a short, dash-gapped run and the exact orange-to-white handoff pixel is ambiguous. The coordinate given is a reasonable midpoint of the observed convergence, explicitly NOT a precision measurement, and should not be treated as more accurate than +/-0.15 degrees. No attempt was made to smooth or regularize this corner into a 'cleaner' shape.
properties.verified_against: Both parts rendered as an overlay on the source figure (2026-09-10) and visually confirmed to closely track the orange dashed line; Part A's shared NW edge visually confirmed identical to Shear Zone's already-approved zone 6/7 boundary; Part B's wedge shape (vertex vertex vertex) visually confirmed against a 2x-upscaled crop of zones 18/19

properties.source_full: Oncel, A.O. and Wilson, T. (2004), Correlation of seismotectonic variables and GPS strain measurements in western Turkey, J. Geophys. Res., 109, B11306, doi:10.1029/2004JB003101
properties.figure: Figure 1 (left panel, geographic map with Shear/Extensional/Compressional Zone outlines)
properties.provenance: This geometry is a RECONSTRUCTION of the white-dashed 'Compressional Zone' outline visible in the published Figure 1 raster, not the authors' original GIS/digitizing data. Produced from the same calibrated, north-up render and calibration used for Shear Zone and Extensional Zone. The white line color (RGB 255,255,255, tight tolerance 20) is heavily confounded in this figure by other white elements (zone-number label boxes, magnitude-event star symbols, white event-date text such as 'Mw 5.6 / 1996', and the legend box) -- these were separated from genuine boundary dashes using connected-component AREA filtering (label boxes and the legend box are large, ~2000-450000 px; individual line dashes are small, 150-1500 px), and candidate dash clusters were additionally cross-checked against zoomed visual crops before being accepted as geometry. No smoothing, interpolation, or geometric regularization was applied beyond selecting representative points through genuinely dense, consistent dash clusters (as was already done for Shear Zone's coastal segments).
properties.geometry_method: calibrated pixel tracing (same 2004_geo_panel_rot.png render/calibration as Shear and Extensional Zones); white line isolated via tight-tolerance color threshold + connected-component area filtering (150-1500 px kept; label boxes, legend, and margin/frame blobs >1500 px or belonging to known non-geometry components excluded); path reconstructed via nearest-neighbor chaining between dash centroids with gap-tolerance breaks, corrected in two places after visual review (see known_limitation)
properties.topology_note: Traces as ONE single closed ring (Polygon, not MultiPolygon) enclosing zones 20,21,22,23,24,25 -- unlike the Extensional Zone, this boundary does not split into disconnected touching pieces; it is one continuous dashed line the whole way around.
properties.confidence: mixed -- see vertex_notes for per-segment confidence (high/medium-high/medium)
properties.known_limitation: (1) A cluster of 8 candidate points near zones 24/25 (approx lon 24.1-24.8, lat 34.6-34.9) was IDENTIFIED AS TEXT CONTAMINATION from the white 'Mw 5.6 / 1996' event label (confirmed by a 2.5x visual crop showing the actual boundary running smoothly along the peninsula's north edge with no real notch there) and was explicitly EXCLUDED from the geometry -- the boundary is represented as a direct, unembellished connection across this gap (vertex indices 37-39) and should be treated as medium-confidence coastal smoothing, not a precision measurement. (2) The zone 22/23 zigzag (vertex indices 9-13) required manual re-sorting by longitude after an initial nearest-neighbor pass produced a self-crossing path; the corrected order was visually confirmed against the source image. (3) Cross-check finding relevant to Extensional Zone: the shared alternating orange/white dashed edge between Extensional and Compressional near the NW corner (vertex indices 0-5) was found to extend continuously from about lon 27.57 to lon 28.95 at lat~36.7-36.75, i.e. further east than the Extensional Zone Part B closing vertex (27.8, 36.7) alone suggested. Per user decision (2026-09-10), the already-approved Extensional Zone geometry (commit abdc307) was deliberately NOT revised based on this finding -- Extensional Part B's own ring already closes consistently on its own terms, and this Compressional-side observation does not by itself prove Extensional's boundary must trace the full shared-edge extent. Flagged here for future reference only.
properties.verified_against: Full ring rendered as an overlay on the source figure (2026-09-10) and visually confirmed to closely track the white dashed line around all of zones 20-25, including the zone 22/23 zigzag and the zone 25 peninsula wrap, with the text-contamination points removed
